subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What are the main purposes of mitosis in the body?
questions.explain: Mitosis is used for growth, repair/replacement of cells, and asexual reproduction.

questions.q: What is the correct order of structures in a reflex arc?
options: Stimulus → receptor → sensory → relay → motor → effector → response
Stimulus → effector → motor → relay → sensory → receptor
questions.explain: The reflex arc runs stimulus, receptor, sensory neurone, relay neurone, motor neurone, effector, response.

options: A cell dividing into two identical cells
A cell becoming specialised for a particular function
questions.explain: Differentiation is the process by which cells become specialised for a specific job.

questions.q: During which stage of the cell cycle do the chromosomes line up in the middle and separate to opposite ends of the cell?
questions.explain: In mitosis the duplicated chromosomes line up and are pulled to opposite poles before the cell divides.

options: They are protective and help prevent injury
questions.explain: Reflexes are fast and protective, for example pulling your hand away from a hot object.

options: An undifferentiated cell that can divide to form different types of cell
A cell that can no longer divide
A cell that has lost its nucleus
questions.explain: Stem cells are undifferentiated cells able to divide and differentiate into specialised cells.

questions.q: What two organs make up the central nervous system (CNS)?
questions.explain: The CNS consists of the brain and spinal cord, which coordinate the body's responses.

questions.q: Why are the new cells made by mitosis described as 'identical'?
options: They are the same size as gametes
They have the same genetic information (DNA) as the parent cell
They have the same shape only
questions.explain: Mitosis copies the DNA exactly, so daughter cells have identical genetic information.

questions.q: Which of these is an ethical concern raised against the use of embryonic stem cells?
options: Embryos that could develop into a person are destroyed
They are too easy to grow
questions.explain: A key objection is that obtaining embryonic stem cells involves destroying embryos.

questions.q: A risk of using stem cells in medical treatment is that:
options: Cultured cells may become contaminated with a virus and pass it to the patient
They cannot divide in the body
questions.explain: Stem cells grown in the lab may be contaminated with viruses that could be transferred to the patient.

questions.q: The two cells produced by mitosis are:
questions.explain: Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells.

questions.q: Which part of the eye changes shape to focus light on the retina?
questions.explain: The lens changes shape (accommodation) to focus light from near or distant objects onto the retina.
